sourceType: Independent original practice questions based on publicly listed exam or MCQ topics; not verbatim UNISA paper questions
sourceLimitations: These are newly written MCQs based on themes in the linked public source, not exact original paper wording. Some source previews are incomplete. Use the Source link to view the original where available.

questions.text: Which business goal is supported when an information system helps staff complete the same work with fewer resources?
questions.explanation:
Operational excellence means using better processes to reduce waste, improve productivity and provide consistent service.

Student note: Think of saving time and reducing errors in the business process.

questions.text: Which group contains major business reasons for investing in information systems?
options: Better decisions, efficient operations and competitive advantage
More paper forms, isolated teams and slower service
Less accurate data and higher transaction costs
Eliminating all competition and avoiding customers
questions.correctAnswer: Better decisions, efficient operations and competitive advantage
questions.explanation:
Businesses use information systems to improve operations, offer new services, build relationships, make better decisions and survive in competitive markets.

Student note: Do not confuse business objectives with the hardware used to achieve them.

questions.text: A company gathers sales facts, processes them and produces useful performance reports. What does this flow illustrate?
options: Turning raw data into valuable information
Transferring ownership of all data to customers
questions.correctAnswer: Turning raw data into valuable information
questions.explanation:
Data is collected, organised and analysed so it becomes information that supports decisions.

Student note: Data is raw facts; information is data with useful meaning.

questions.text: Why do enterprise applications connect departments such as sales, finance and inventory?
options: To share information and support processes across the business
To force each department to maintain unrelated records
To replace all suppliers with employees
questions.correctAnswer: To share information and support processes across the business
questions.explanation:
Enterprise systems allow different departments to work with consistent shared data instead of isolated information.

Student note: Remember ERP = integrated business processes and shared information.

questions.text: A company wants selected external customers to see their advertising performance reports securely. Which network is designed for controlled access by outside partners?
questions.explanation:
An extranet extends approved parts of a company's system or network to authorised external users.

Student note: Intranet is mainly internal; extranet allows selected outsiders.

questions.text: Which item is not one of Porter's five competitive forces?
questions.explanation:
The five forces consider industry rivalry, customers, suppliers, substitutes and potential new entrants.

Student note: The five forces describe competition, not a list of computer tools.

questions.text: What is a core competence in business strategy?
options: An activity the company performs exceptionally well
Any task outsourced to another company
A law that every employee must learn
The number of servers in the company
questions.correctAnswer: An activity the company performs exceptionally well
questions.explanation:
Core competencies are strengths that can help a firm stand out and create value.

Student note: A company can use IT to strengthen its core competence.

options: Software whose source code can be viewed and modified under its licence
Software that never needs security updates
Any software that is always free to run commercially
Software stored only on one company's private server
questions.correctAnswer: Software whose source code can be viewed and modified under its licence
questions.explanation:
Open-source licences generally allow people to inspect and modify source code, subject to licence rules.

Student note: Open-source does not mean there are no licence conditions or maintenance costs.

questions.text: Which tool does a person normally use to request and display a website?
questions.explanation:
A browser requests web resources and shows them to people using a graphical interface.

Student note: Chrome and Firefox are browsers; Apache and Nginx are servers.

questions.text: When a company hires an outside specialist to build or maintain its software, what is this called?
questions.explanation:
Outsourcing transfers a defined service or development task to an outside provider under an agreement.

Student note: Distinguish outsourcing from using software developed internally.
